taxonomic_note: Canonical spelling corrected to Yucca treculiana Carrière following the current Kew/POWO 2026 backbone. Many Texas floras, databases, and the source pool use Yucca treculeana. Current Kew separately accepts Y. torreyi; older FNA lumped Y. torreyi into Y. treculeana.
look_here_first: This is the other large tree yucca in the batch. Look for a branched or few-trunked crown of broad rigid leaves that are traditionally mostly without marginal threads and not rolled inward at the tip, then confirm with the stouter ovary and fleshy pendant fruit.
project_tracker_diagnostic: arborescent/tree-like, often several meters tall and sometimes branched; broad thick rigid leaves forming terminal crowns; traditional Texas key: leaf margins mostly without marginal threads and leaf tips not strongly inrolled; traditional key: stout ovary about 7–12 mm diameter at flowering; dense cream to greenish-cream flower panicle; large pendant fleshy succulent indehiscent fruit

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bexar — a 2025 TCEQ Edwards Aquifer site assessment in Bexar County records Yucca treculeana on the project site; this is the widespread older spelling of the currently accepted Y. treculiana. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list for Travis County includes Trecul yucca under Yucca treculeana. Burnet — field documentation from Double Eagle Ranch in Burnet County records several wild communities of Yucca treculeana/treculiana.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yucca torreyi: Traditional Texas keys separate Y. treculiana by mostly non-filiferous, non-inrolled leaf tips and a stouter ovary, versus Y. torreyi with marginal threads, inrolled apical leaf margins, and a more slender ovary. Use multiple characters because older FNA lumped the taxa and historical hybridization has been reported. Yucca aloifolia: Both are tree yuccas with dagger leaves, but Y. treculiana belongs to the Texas/Mexico fleshy-fruited complex and should be checked by fruit, leaf margin architecture, flower morphology, and geographic range rather than generic 'Spanish dagger' appearance.
